findings.title: Exact comparisons made progress measurable
findings.body: The comparison records the entire parse or check result: whether the program is accepted, where an error occurs, its phase and its diagnostics. Grammar and source-origin repairs closed 116 differences while keeping every previous match and all 919 positive programs. That makes the graph useful for tracking both everyday usability and language behavior.

findings.title: Smaller values also made checking more reliable
findings.body: Compact natural numbers and simpler descent eliminated deep-literal failures and a negative-test timeout. Avoiding extra call wrappers then removed a long-string stack overflow under the same resource limits. The exact-match curve moves only four rows across these releases, but those rows represent programs that changed from failing or timing out to the intended result.

findings.title: Shared error rendering improved the developer experience
findings.body: One diagnostic renderer restored source carets consistently, and missing-import handling retained the right error context. Together with malformed-binder handling, the release added 144 exact matches without losing an earlier match. These improvements make errors easier to locate and keep the Bend compiler familiar to users of the reference implementation.

findings.title: Keeping source information early avoided guessing later
findings.body: The compiler attached source origins when terms were created and carried them through later transformations. Parser and checker checkpoints also became explicit. This let the compiler select the same error at the same point as the reference, closing 457 differences with no lost matches. Compact literal representation kept this richer information affordable.

findings.title: One contextual frontend closed the remaining gaps
findings.body: Parsing now carries lexical scope, aliases, namespaces and fresh-name state when they are needed. A shared materializer performs semantic work at the correct early or deferred checkpoint. This replaces reconstruction paths that could choose the wrong error or scope. It closes the final main-suite differences and every remaining difference in the frozen broader selection.

findings.title: Nearby examples turned a near-perfect score into stronger evidence
findings.body: When the main corpus was already 99.93% exact, targeted neighboring examples still exposed scope, grouping and declaration-order gaps. Keeping that 196-observation selection separate made those weaknesses visible. Fixes raised it from 128 to 136, then 139, then 196 exact observations, improving behavior beyond the original headline score.

findings.title: Exactness survived an expanded upstream target
findings.body: The next upstream update added 15 fixtures, including deep shared-equality regressions. Graph-conversion, Base and backend migration retained exact main and broader frontend results. The larger denominator therefore marks added coverage, and the later release continues to match the same pinned target.

findings.title: Execution checks found bugs that frontend checks could not see
findings.body: A separate execution pilot exposed foreign/constructor name collisions and distinct source names colliding in emitted C. A shared emission check and unambiguous native identifiers repaired those implementation defects. Keeping execution coverage separate let the project improve generated code even after frontend comparisons had reached zero differences.

findings.title: Performance work now ships with preserved behavior
findings.body: The installed Phase36 compiler keeps exact frontend agreement and passes all 42 ordinary and relocated CLI checks. Seven new control groups exercise scoped proof reuse, callback reentry, produced trees, aliases and selectors. These checks bind the latest optimizations to actual emitted programs and complement the inherited execution and library controls.

findings.title: The private backend retains the tested frontend contract
findings.metric: 3,026 main + 196 broader exact; 42 CLI checks pass
findings.body: Installed worker23 keeps exact frontend agreement and all 81 retained backend outcomes, including the original shared failures and unavailable cases. Eight maintained suites and fresh composition controls pass; separate mechanism controls cover bounded fallback, tail transfer, Number-Nat bounds, mutable public descriptors and immutable results. These overlapping finite checks support the installed optimization without turning selected coverage into universal conformance.

findings.title: Independent source expectations exposed a bug shared comparisons could miss
findings.body: Direct06 and pinned TypeScript both failed an unchanged signaling-NaN oracle, with different wrong results. Writing directly into fresh typed-array storage preserves the tested payloads on cold calls and raises the candidate to 96 passing source scenarios. The reference remains at 95, so reproducing its erroneous result is not counted as correctness. Separate composition controls retain callback order, demand, captures and genuine overapplication.
